introduction: The marriage registration process in Tamil Nadu is centrally managed by the Registration Department through the TNREGINET portal under the Tamil Nadu Registration of Marriages Act, 2009.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Portal Used: TNREGINET (Tamil Nadu Registration Department).
  • Applicable Acts: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and Tamil Nadu Marriage Act. (Process demonstrated for Hindu Marriage Act).
  • Age Eligibility: Bridegroom must be 21+ years old; Bride must be 18+ years old.
  • Religious Eligibility (Hindu Act): Both partners must be Hindu, Buddhist, or Sikh.
  • Platform Restriction: Must be accessed via a desktop or laptop; mobile browsers are not supported.
  • Mandatory Physical Visit: Both partners and witnesses must visit the Sub-Registrar's office in person to complete registration.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Marriage Registration

Requirement: You must upload the designated documents online and carry the originals plus 2 sets of photocopies during your offline visit.
For Husband & Wife
  • ID Proof: Aadhaar Card.
  • Age Proof: School Certificates (10th, 12th, or College Transfer Certificate / Marksheet). If unavailable, submit Birth Certificate or PAN card.
  • Address Proof: Ration Card (Address must match Aadhaar card exactly).
  • Community Certificate: Mandatory under Hindu Marriage Act to verify religion/caste (No online upload needed, carry original offline).
  • Photographs: 6 passport-size photographs of the husband and 6 of the wife.
For Witnesses (Usually Parents)
  • ID/Address Proof: Aadhaar Card for the parents of both the husband and the wife.
Additional Items for SRO Office Visit
  • 2 printed copies of the completed Online Application Form (usually 6 to 7 pages).
  • 2 printed copies of the Payment Receipt.
  • 2 printed copies of the Appointment Token.
  • A CD containing video/photos of the marriage ceremony (often requested by the registrar).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application & Appointment Booking

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Portal Registration: Go to tnreginet.gov.in on a computer. Create a user ID using your phone number, Aadhaar, and email, and log in.
  2. Start Application: Navigate to Registration -> Registration of Marriage -> Registration under Hindu Marriage Act.
  3. Marriage Details: Enter the exact date, month, and year the marriage took place.
  4. Husband & Wife Details: Fill in names exactly as they appear on the Aadhaar card. Enter Date of Birth, religion, caste (must exactly match the Community Certificate), marital status (Bachelor/Spinster), occupation, and address.
  5. Parents & Witnesses: Fill in details for both sets of parents. The system allows you to select parents to act as default witnesses. Enter their Aadhaar details and addresses.
  6. Venue & Registrar Selection: Enter the details of who solemnized the marriage (e.g., fathers' names) and the exact address of the temple or marriage hall. Select the local Sub-Registrar office corresponding to that jurisdiction. Specify how many copies of the certificate you want (usually 2).
  7. Document Upload: Select your proof types (Aadhaar, Ration Card, School Cert) and carefully type in the exact document identification numbers (e.g., Aadhaar number, Marksheet serial number). Any typos here will cause rejection during physical verification. Save the application.
  8. Payment: Click "Proceed for Payment". Select an online payment gateway (like SBI Gateway), pay the registration and copy fees (Net banking, UPI, or Debit/Credit card), and download the PDF Payment Receipt. Do not just click "OK" without downloading the PDF.
  9. Initiate Token: Go to Search Applications, enter your application number, and click "Initiate Token." Choose an available date (marked in green) and a time slot for your office visit. Download the Token Acknowledgment PDF.
  10. Download Application: From the same Search Applications menu, download the final generated Application PDF.
  11. The Offline Visit: On your appointment date and time, the husband, wife, and witnesses (parents) must visit the Sub-Registrar's office. Take all original documents, xerox sets, photos, and printed application/receipts. Do not affix the photos or sign the printed application at home. You must paste the photos and sign the documents directly in front of the Registrar.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Application (Manual Registration)

Note: While Tamil Nadu allows manual registration, online initiation is highly preferred by the government.
Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Visit SRO Office: Visit the Sub-Registrar's office under whose jurisdiction the marriage took place or where either partner has resided for more than six months.
  2. Obtain Form: Obtain the physical Marriage Registration Application Form (Form I) from the office.
  3. Fill Out Manually: Fill out the application manually with the details of the couple, parents, witnesses, and the venue of the marriage.
  4. Attach Photocopies: Attach physical photocopies of all required documents (Age proof, Address proof, ID proof, Community certificate, and wedding invitation/proof) and passport-size photographs.
  5. Submit and Pay: Submit the file to the Sub-Registrar and pay the registration fees in cash or via demand draft at the counter.
  6. Verification Schedule: The office will assign a date for physical verification, where the couple and witnesses must appear in person to sign the official register.
afterApplying:
After SRO Visit & Verification

Once the offline physical verification is complete, original documents are checked, and signatures are recorded at the Sub-Registrar office:

  • Approval: The application will be officially approved by the Sub-Registrar.
  • Certificate Issuance: The final, legally valid Marriage Certificate will be issued. Standard timelines range from 3 days to 1 week (maximum 15 days).
  • Collection & Download: You will be asked to collect the physical copies directly from the office, or you can download the digitally signed certificate from your TNREGINET dashboard.
